title: Implement Newton-John / M4RM-style GEMM for GF(2^8)
description:
Close the GF(2^8) algorithmic gap to M4RIE via Newton-John / Method of Four Russians.

## Background

Per `dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-e24f7839-panelized-gf2m-gemm.md` § 4 and `dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-a1172cea-gf2m-scorecard.md` § 4, GF(2^8) matmul against M4RIE shows a structural algorithmic gap that panelized GEMM (e24f7839) cannot close:

- GF(2^8) n=64: gf2 1.593e9 ops/s vs M4RIE 4.052e9 ops/s (ratio 0.393, threshold 0.667)
- GF(2^8) n=256: gf2 1.470e9 ops/s vs M4RIE 2.453e10 ops/s (ratio 0.060)
- GF(2^8) n=1024: gf2 1.437e9 ops/s vs M4RIE 9.757e10 ops/s (ratio 0.015)

M4RIE GF(2^8) throughput scales 4.1 -> 97.6 Gop/s from n=64 to n=1024 (24x), confirming it uses an O(n^3/log n) algorithm. gf2-core's per-element CLMUL is O(n^3) and stays flat at ~1.5 Gop/s.

## Algorithm

M4RIE-class Newton-John / Method of Four Russians for GF(2^8):
1. Pack the right-hand matrix B into byte form (256 distinct values per byte).
2. Precompute 16 word-level multiplication tables (one per nibble pair) using PSHUFB.
3. The inner loop processes each row of A as a packed-byte vector and uses PSHUFB lookups to multiply against the precomputed table panels of B.
4. Accumulate XORs across the panels.

The reference implementation is M4RIE's `mzed_mul` source. Reading m4rie source plus the algorithm paper is the recommended starting point.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] GF(2^8) FieldMatrix GEMM target rows at n in {64, 256, 1024} reach >= 0.667 of M4RIE throughput on the Zen-3 host class.
- [hard] Bit-exact equivalence with the existing CLMUL path on randomized inputs (seed-controlled property tests).
- [hard] No unsafe code outside `gf2-kernels-simd`. The new kernel may use AVX2 PSHUFB intrinsics inside the kernel crate; gf2-core remains `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.
- [hard] No regression on GF(2^16) or GF(2^32) panelized GEMM (cells already passing in e24f7839).

## Notes

- This task is non-blocking on epic 97bf0879. It is a follow-up to e24f7839 closure (Wave-8 amendment 2026-05-06). The epic closure path proceeds without this work.
- The follow-up may overlap with a future GFNI / AVX-512 lane (`fb271c41` decision deferred those to Zen-4+ host classes); coordinate before dispatch.
- Successor epic candidate: if Newton-John lands but other GF(2^m) optimization gaps surface, those move to a successor epic of `97bf0879`.
